otherProblems: In the stress frame (G-2.png) the right-hand team name wraps to two lines while the left-hand name stays on one, so the two sides are given visibly unequal width and the board reads a little lopsided; all text stays inside the panel though.

Under stress the panel grows to hold the long names and big scores; the only wrinkle is that the right-hand name wraps while the left does not, which makes the sides slightly unequal, but it remains clean and legible, so a director would take it as delivered.

A clean, well-composed lower-left music bug: a dark translucent panel with an orange left accent, a small "NOW PLAYING" kicker with a short rule that starts after the text rather than touching it, a large bold title, a lighter artist line, and a waveform-style 0–100 progress with an orange played portion and playhead that reads clearly as the progress element. otherProblems: The 'GOAL' flag banner hangs a few pixels below the main panel as a separate block rather than being joined to it; a small seam a viewer might notice but not a broken look.

Plain, but balanced and readable enough to air as delivered.

Panel sits very low and tight to the left edge of a 1920x1080 frame, close to the title-safe margin.

basicMistakes.where: The vertical gradient accent bar at the left edge of the text column sits directly on the first letter 'I' of INGRID BAKKER and the 'P' of POLLING ANALYST, with zero gap — the bar runs over the leading glyphs.

otherProblems: No left padding between the accent bar and the text block, so the name and title read as jammed against the bar while the logo cell has generous padding — uneven padding across the panel.

The logo is a plain italic underlined wordmark; acceptable, but the thin divider rule beside it adds little and its lower end fades unevenly.
answer.reasons: The panel is dark, legible and the stress values grow the panel cleanly without clipping, which is good. otherProblems: The brief requires very long names to be carried without wrapping; the name wraps to two lines in G-1 and three lines in G-2, and the title wraps to two lines in G-2.

The 'KSTRL' logo floats in a large, otherwise empty left box of its own, apart from the text, on a mismatched lighter panel.

The whole piece is a dark near-black strap with a neon-green sports wordmark rather than the conservative navy strap the news-desk brief asks for; the panel also stops at ~1210px with an uneven right margin behind the title box.
answer.reasons: Nothing is clipped or unreadable, but the graphic fails the brief and the desk check: the name wraps (to three lines under stress) when the brief says it must not, an empty black band with a stray 'K' is stacked above the strap with a misaligned accent, and the logo sits alone in a large empty box apart from the text. basicMistakes.where: Name line "Ravi Chandrasekaran de la Cruz" runs to the panel's right edge and the final "z" is cut mid-glyph by the panel mask, leaving "Cru" with a sliced letter.

otherProblems: Role line in light grey on off-white is on the faint side for the subordinate text, though still legible at this size.

answer.reasons: The settled frame is clean and on-brief: stark off-white plate, bold black name, two-line grey role clearly subordinate, small newspaper mark sitting flush with the text. But the stress frame breaks: the longer name hits the fixed panel edge and the last glyph is sliced off mid-letter with no ellipsis or fit-to-width, which a viewer would see immediately. That is a basic clipping fault and keeps it off air as delivered.

otherProblems: A dashed placeholder box labelled "LOGO" floats on air above the name in both frames (G-1 at ~x300-365, y605-690; G-2 at ~x595-660), unattached to the text and repositioning itself with the name width - an unfinished placeholder a viewer would see.

A second logo (newspaper icon) sits on its own white square at lower-left, above and to the left of the name rather than aligned with it, beside an orphaned vertical rule (x~240, y715-810) with nothing to its right - furniture stacked above the lower third that reads as an accident.
Two competing logo elements on one lower third contradict the brief's minimalist, no-panel typographic discipline.
Title line is mid-grey on a dark plate; it is readable here but is not the high contrast the brief asks for over footage.
answer.reasons: The typography itself is sound: name and title are legible, the short underline is clean, and the stress values fit inside the frame without clipping. But the graphic ships with a visible dashed "LOGO" placeholder box hovering over the name, plus a separate newspaper icon on its own white square sitting beside an empty vertical rule above the text. That is a floating logo on a box, a second logo apart from the text, and decorative furniture stacked above the lower third - all things a viewer would see, and the placeholder alone makes it read as unfinished. A director would not take this to air as delivered.

basicMistakes.where: The vertical black divider rule at the left of the text column sits on the first glyphs of 'Ravi' and 'Professor' — the R and P start flush against/under the rule with no left padding.
The same divider rule overlaps the left strokes of 'Ravi', 'Whittington' and 'Southern'; the text column has zero inset from the rule.

otherProblems: The logo cell is a generic document icon rather than a brand mark, and reads as a placeholder; it is also larger relative to the name than the stark typographic brief wants.
Name wraps to two lines in the stress frame while the panel keeps the same height proportion, so the block grows tall and the subordinate role line is squeezed close to the bottom edge.
answer.reasons: The structure is sensible — ink-on-paper white card, bold black name, grey subordinate role, stress values carried by wrapping without clipping — but the text column has no left inset, so the black divider rule sits directly on the first letters of the name and role in both frames. A rule touching or overlapping text is a basic mistake a viewer would see on every take, so it does not air as delivered.

otherProblems: The Sunbeam sun mark sits on a dark navy plate of its own, a hard rectangle inset in the cream panel that fights the warm brand and reads as a logo box rather than part of the strap.

Layout is the reverse of the brief: the channel mark is on the left and the circular portrait is not on the left of the strap but a small disc floating above the name, with the top of the panel otherwise empty beside it.
The portrait disc is small and out of proportion to the strap, and the title line is small for daytime television.
The orange accent along the top edge fades out partway across and looks unfinished rather than designed.
answer.reasons: Text is clean and readable in both frames, the stress values fit inside the panel with no clipping or collisions, so there are no basic mistakes. But the logo sits on a dark box of its own inside the warm cream panel, the portrait is a small disc hovering above the name instead of a circular portrait area on the left, and the channel mark is on the wrong side; the strap reads as pieces placed rather than a designed Sunbeam lower third. A director would send it back rather than air it as delivered.

otherProblems: Stress frame: the wrapped name's two lines sit with tight leading and the first line ends on a dangling hyphen — legible and contained, but a slightly ungainly break.
Title line is on the small side for a television, though still readable against the dark panel.
answer.reasons: A clean, on-brief lower third: dark club-neutral panel, vivid lime angled slash separating the KSTRL wordmark from condensed bold white name and grey title, all inside the panel with even padding. Under stress the panel grows to carry the two-line name and the long title with no clipping, overlap or contrast loss. The only quibbles are the tight leading on the wrapped name and a smallish title line, neither of which a director would hold it for.

otherProblems: The light panel is roughly 310px tall but the name and title occupy only its top band; the lower half of the panel is empty, so the text reads as pushed into the top of an otherwise empty box (G-1.png and G-2.png).
The newspaper logo sits below and apart from the text block, left of the text column and above a large void, rather than aligned with the name/title group (both frames).
The panel's bottom edge is uneven: a small stepped notch at the lower-left corner where the panel ends at a different height than the rest, which looks like a rendering accident (both frames).

The brief asked for no panel, a stark typographic treatment with a short underline over footage; the delivered graphic is a large solid card with no underline, the opposite of the brief's minimalist documentary direction.
In G-1 the narrow panel is nearly square and the proportions look odd for a lower third; the panel grows wide in G-2 but keeps the same large empty lower area.
answer.reasons: The text itself is clean, high-contrast and survives the stress values without clipping, so there is no basic mistake. But the graphic is a large light card with the name and title crammed into its top, a logo floating loose beneath them, and about half the panel left empty, plus a stepped notch on the bottom edge that reads as a bug. That layout, together with ignoring the brief's no-panel/underline direction, is not something a director would put on air as delivered.

basicMistakes.where: The placeholder label inside the orange portrait circle is cut by the circle mask — only 'ortrait' shows, with the 'P' and the top of the word sliced off, at the top-left of the circle above the name.
Same clipped 'ortrait' label at the top of the orange portrait circle, above the stress name.

otherProblems: The Sunbeam sun logo sits on a tall dark navy plate of its own inside the cream strap — a logo on a box, and the plate reads as a heavy, alien block against the warm cream panel.
The channel mark is on the left of the strap and the portrait circle is stacked above the name text, the reverse of the brief's layout (circular portrait area left, channel mark right).
The orange portrait circle crowds the name line with almost no clearance, and the stress frame leaves a large empty cream area to the right of the circle, so the panel reads unbalanced.
answer.reasons: The portrait circle carries a text label that is clipped mid-glyph by the circle mask in both frames, which alone keeps it off air. Beyond that, the channel logo sits on a dark box of its own on the wrong side of the strap, the portrait circle is stacked over the name instead of at the left, and the composition reads as unresolved rather than a warm, settled daytime strap. The stress values do fit the panel cleanly, but the clipped label and the logo plate are faults a viewer and any director would see immediately.

basicMistakes.where: Label 'Introduction to Broadcast Graphics begins in' and the 10:00 timer, centre of frame — pale grey text with no plate on a mid-grey background, barely distinguishable
Two-line stress label and the 14:48:00 timer, centre of frame — same washed-out grey-on-grey, no backing panel
Label and the 9:59 timer, centre of frame — same near-invisible contrast after pause

Label in G-1 wraps into two lines at a modest size for a 'back of the lecture hall' requirement.

basicMistakes.where: The role panel 'SENIOR EUROPEAN ECONOMICS CORRESPONDENT' sits directly on top of the name; only 'Alex' is visible and the rest of 'Alexandra Konstantopoulos-Vandermeulen' shows through as ghosted text behind the role box, lower-left panel.

otherProblems: The role box is a separate, misaligned plate that overhangs the main panel in the stress frame, reading as a layout accident rather than a design.
The brief's very long name is never legible in either frame — the graphic fails its core requirement of carrying the name without leaving the panel.
answer.reasons: The role field is drawn on top of the name field in both frames, so the speaker's name is unreadable beyond its first few letters — a straightforward text-over-text collision that is visible even with the brief's own values. Under stress the role box also spills past the main panel's right edge and the name is truncated mid-word with no ellipsis. The gold accent bar and dark panel are fine in themselves, but the graphic cannot show the one thing a lower third exists to show.

basicMistakes.where: The grey footer line '18,204 votes counted · Voting closes at 20:45' sits directly on top of the white question text 'Which change would improve your commute most?' in the panel header.
The doubled footer line '18,204 votes counted · Voting closes at 20:45 …' runs straight through both lines of the doubled question text in the header.
The footer line escapes the right edge of the dark panel and continues over the studio plate ('…Voting closes at' past x≈1020), with its wrapped tail '20:45' hidden behind the question text.

otherProblems: Every option reads '0%' while the bars show clearly different fills, so the numbers and bars contradict each other and the leader is not shown ahead by its percentage.
A band of empty panel below the last option in both frames makes the bottom padding read as broken.

On top of that the percentages all read 0% against bars of differing length, so the live numbers the brief asks for are not actually shown. The layout, type and bar treatment are otherwise clean, but as delivered this cannot go to air.

basicMistakes.where: Government clock in the left panel reads '3:0' with the final digit cut mid-glyph by the clock field's mask.
Government clock in the left panel reads '14:' with the following digits cut mid-glyph; the stress clock value does not fit the field.
Government clock in the left panel reads '2:5' with the last digit cut mid-glyph after the switch.

basicMistakes.where: Name line 'Alexandra Konstantopoulos-Vandermeulen' is cut mid-glyph after 'Konstantopoul' at about x=795, well inside the dark panel (which runs to x≈1260); the rest of the name never appears.
Both name lines are cut mid-glyph after 'Konstantopoul' at about x=795 inside a panel that is now ~1385px wide; the name field is masked far narrower than the panel.

In the stress frame the name wraps to two lines yet is still truncated on each line, so the wrap does nothing to rescue it.
answer.reasons: The panel, rule and red accent are calm and well-proportioned, and the role line sits cleanly even under stress, but the name — the one thing the brief insists on — is sheared mid-letter at 'Konstantopoul' in both frames with a large empty stretch of panel to its right. A viewer would see a hacked-off name with no ellipsis; the brief's own value never appears in full. That is a basic clipping fault and it does not air.

basicMistakes.where: Team names, scores and the 'LIVE' label are light grey on a mid-grey translucent panel, top-left; the text is only a shade lighter than the plate and would not read on a television.
'FULL TIME', 'LIONS LIONS', '888 888' and 'FALCONS FALCONS' in the same washed grey-on-grey, top-left panel.

otherProblems: In the stress frame the right team name wraps to two lines while the left stays on one, so the two names sit at different heights and the board reads lopsided.

No frame shows a goal flag, so that moment cannot be assessed from what was delivered.

The stress frame also handles long names unevenly, with one side wrapping to two lines and the other not, leaving the two teams misaligned. Beyond the contrast, it is an unstyled grey box with no visual hierarchy for the scores.

basicMistakes.where: All text on the scoreboard (team names, scores, 'FIRST HALF') is muted grey on a translucent grey panel over a grey/beige plate — the whole board reads as washed-out and near-illegible, 'FIRST HALF' especially.
Same low-contrast grey-on-grey text across the board, the 'FULL TIME FULL TIME' status line and the detached 'GOAL GOAL' band.

otherProblems: The entire panel is so translucent and desaturated it looks like a disabled or preview state rather than a live graphic.
'FIRST HALF' / 'FULL TIME' status text is tiny and faint for a television viewer.

The goal flag is a separate grey block floating under the board with a gap, reading as detached furniture rather than part of the scoreboard; the orange accent rule sits tight under the second team's wrapped name.
answer.reasons: The layout itself is sensible — two name rows, score cells, a status strip, names wrap cleanly under stress and scores fit — but the whole board is grey text on a ghosted grey panel with almost no contrast, so a viewer could not read names, scores or the status line on a television. That alone keeps it off air. The detached goal band and the faint, tiny status text add to a graphic that looks unfinished rather than designed.

otherProblems: Under one minute (G-2, 00:41) the change of gear is carried only by the status badge and sub-line copy ('TERMINAL COUNT', 'FINAL SEQUENCE INITIATED'); the clock itself keeps the same size, weight and colour, so the shift is quieter than the brief's 'visibly change gear' asks for.
The panel widens leftward to fit the stress label, which is fine, but the layout then has the badge sitting far from the right-aligned 'BOREAL LIVE' wordmark with a wide empty gap between them.
answer.reasons: A clean, calm, well-proportioned countdown panel: the T- clock is clearly the hero, large and highly legible on the dark green plate, the event label fits on one line in both frames with nothing clipped or overlapping, the rule and progress bar sit clear of the text, and the brand wordmark is just type with no box or odd scale. otherProblems: The card bodies carry a lot of dead space between the place header, the team block and the prize box, so each card reads a little airy for the amount of content it holds.
The three small cyan/pink dashes at the right of the title bar are decorative furniture with no job; a viewer may read them as a progress indicator that never changes.

The brand tag is integrated into the title bar rather than floating. otherProblems: Before the first step (G-1, G-2) the panel keeps its full height with the lower half empty; it reads as reserved answer space rather than an accident, but a tighter question-only state would look more finished.

The three-line stress question wraps inside the panel with no clipping or collisions; badge, rule and corner accents sit clear of all text. otherProblems: Role line is on the small side (~22 px cap height) for a television subtitle, though still legible.
Vertical padding under the name is tight where the role plate overlaps the name plate's bottom edge; a minor nit.
The small magenta sliver at the name plate's lower-right corner is a few pixels and could be read as a stray chip, though it fits the neon offset-layer style.
answer.reasons: A clean, angular esports lower third: the name and role plates grow with their content so both the brief's values and the long stress values sit fully inside their panels with even padding, nothing is clipped, and the cyan top rule and magenta bottom rule stay clear of the text. White-on-navy and cyan-on-navy contrast is strong and the slanted plates with neon edge accents match the Pulse Arena brief. Only small nits remain (slightly small role text, tight bottom padding, a tiny magenta accent chip), none of which a viewer would notice, so it airs as delivered.

otherProblems: Score colouring is inconsistent between frames: in G-1 the away score '0' is white while home '1' is lime, but in G-2 both '12' and '11' are lime - a small oddity a viewer might notice as scores bump.

In the stress frame the bar grows to roughly two-thirds of the frame width, so 'never in the way of play' is stretched, though all text stays inside its cells.
answer.reasons: A compact, single-strip corner scoreboard with a bold condensed face, lime accents and clear cell separation; every field is readable, nothing is clipped or overlapping in either frame, and padding is even. The stress names fit fully inside their cells with the clock and scores intact. The only wrinkles are a small inconsistency in which scores get the lime colour and a wide stress-state bar, neither of which would stop a director taking it to air.
